thread:
liam: Seeing steady memory growth on longpad streaming sessions — KV residency climbs over time even with normal eviction. Repro on staging with 90m continuous tool-loop.
maya: Ugh. Which metric shows it? resident RSS or our kv tracker?
liam: kv_tracker shows active_kv_pages: 192 -> 1040 over 90m. RSS follows roughly +2.1GB. Snapshot: `kv_pages_by_span` shows many small spans not being reclaimed.
nora: can you paste the dumper output?
liam: pastebin: https://p.redwood.internal/kv-dump-2173456789.txt
liam: snippet: ```span:0x7f8a12 size:8 pages:3 last_access:2026-02-14T12:34Z refcount:0 state:stale``` lots of 'stale' but not freed.
axel: Do we still have the old handoff path where stale spans wait for page_coalesce on background sweeper? Might be starving under heavy streaming.
maya: We recently changed kernel selection to favor fused matmul which reduced cores available to sweeper threads on some nodes. Could be correlated.
ora: timeline? when did kernel change land to prod?
liam: rolled 2026-02-12 03:00 UTC. Repro started 02/13 09:00 UTC.
axel: Good lead. If sweeper threads are CPU-starved they won't coalesce fragments -> fragmentation growth -> pages pinned awaiting coalesce.
ora: Any pprof heap/lock profiles from staging during the run?
liam: grabbed a cpu + heap pprof at 60m: `go tool pprof --pdf` shows sweeper goroutines blocked on `kernel_scheduler.WaitForAvail` contended with inference workers.
maya: Could we try bumping sweeper priority or pinning sweeper to a reserved core and see if residency stabilizes? quick experiment on one node should be fast.
liam: spun a test node with sweeper cpuset reserved 1 core, ran 2h stream test. active_kv_pages peaked at 210 then dropped to 70 after coalesce pass. RSS stayed flat.
ora: Nice. That points to scheduling rather than a classic leak.
ora: But why are refcounts stale==0 but not freed? something else must hold page refs transiently.
liam: dug into page_release path — we found `page_handoff_queue` only processed by sweeper; inference code sometimes re-acquires page for pending toolcalls which momentarily increments refcount then drops; if sweeper starved those pages linger in queue behind heavy enqueues.
ora: OK. Action items: 1) revert kernel affinity tweak or reserve core for sweeper, 2) add watchdog to force coalesce if handoff queue > 500, 3) add extra logs for page_handoff_queue depth.
axel: I'll put up a small PR for (2) to force a background drain when queue high. PR link: https://git.redwood/infer/ops/kv/PR-624
maya: Also add a perf test in staging that runs longpad stream for 3h to catch regressions.
ora: Can we add a smoke check in release pipeline to detect >+1GB kv residency over 30m for longpad workload?
liam: Yup, I'll add a smoke metric and a dashboard alert.
perf-bot: Automated test `longpad-kv-stress` failed on staging at 2026-02-14T14:50Z — kv_residency increased 1.8GB over 45m. See CI run 6289.
maya: Thanks. I'll coordinate with infra to roll the sweeper core reservation as a stopgap on the next cluster rollout.
liam: Saved logs and a minimal repro script in the ticket: https://tickets.redwood/internal/INF-3781
nora: Great triage. Let's keep thread updated when PRs land and when staging runs pass.
liam: Filed follow-ups: INF-3781 (investigation), INF-3782 (watchdog PR), INF-3783 (release smoke).
